tasks.title: Buy CT Pros domain + wire real website/email

prep.what: Purchase and configure CT Pros's business domain, then point MX records for their business email.
prep.understand: Domain registrar flow (Namecheap/GoDaddy/Google Domains), DNS record types — MX for email, A/CNAME for website. Email hosting (Google Workspace or similar) requires specific MX values provided by the email provider.
approach: Search and purchase a suitable domain (e.g. ctpros.com or ctpros.net) via the chosen registrar
Point A record to the website host (or a parking page if the site isn't ready yet)
Add MX records for the email provider (Google Workspace: aspmx.l.google.com + priority entries)
Verify DNS propagation has started and document all credentials/registrar login for the client
resources: Domain registrar dashboard (Namecheap / GoDaddy / Google Domains)
Google Workspace admin console — for MX record values
dnschecker.org — verify DNS propagation across regions

tasks.title: Fill real CT Pros company contact info

prep.what: Enter CT Pros's official business details (legal name, address, phone, EIN) into AZ Takeoff so they appear correctly on invoices and QB records.
prep.understand: This data flows downstream into invoice headers, QuickBooks company sync, and client-facing documents — getting it right here avoids a cascade of corrections after go-live.
approach: Open AZ Takeoff company settings / onboarding form for CT Pros
Gather CT Pros's official business registration details (legal name, EIN, full address, phone)
Fill in all required fields — double-check spelling and EIN format (XX-XXXXXXX)
Save and preview an invoice to confirm the header displays correctly
resources: AZ Takeoff company settings panel
CT Pros business registration or W-9 for official details
QB company settings page for cross-reference field format

prep.what: OAuth-connect the live CT Pros QuickBooks account to AZ Takeoff so real invoices and vendor records sync.
prep.understand: QB uses OAuth2 — you need the CT Pros QB account owner to log in during the flow. Production and sandbox QB are separate environments; make sure you're connecting to the production account, not the dev sandbox.
approach: Confirm you have CT Pros QB account owner credentials (or arrange for the client to be present)
Open AZ Takeoff integrations → QuickBooks and click 'Connect QuickBooks'
Complete the OAuth redirect: log in as CT Pros QB owner and authorize the app
Verify the connection shows 'Active' with the correct company name before closing
resources: AZ Takeoff QB integration settings page
CT Pros QuickBooks login credentials (confirm with client beforehand)
Intuit developer OAuth2 docs — for debugging redirect or scope errors

prep.what: Push a test takeoff job end-to-end through the QB sync and confirm the invoice lands correctly in QuickBooks with the right line items, amounts, and customer mapping.
prep.understand: You're validating the full data pipeline: AZ Takeoff job → invoice object → QB API → QB books. The sandbox uses Intuit's developer QB environment — separate credentials from production. Watch for field mismatches: line item names, customer IDs, tax codes.
approach: Set up a test job in AZ Takeoff using the sandbox QB connection
Generate an invoice from the test job and trigger the QB sync
Log in to QB sandbox and locate the new invoice — check customer, line items, amounts, tax
Check AZ Takeoff sync logs for errors and document any field mismatches to resolve before production cutover
resources: AZ Takeoff invoice/sync logs panel
QuickBooks sandbox: developer.intuit.com → your sandbox company
QB Invoice API object schema (for line item field names and required fields)
AZ Takeoff QB integration error codes / documentation

tasks.title: Label lane v2 M3 vision for outlined-text firms

prep.what: Spec the updated label-lane detection strategy for firms whose blueprints use outlined (hollow) text instead of solid-filled text.
prep.understand: The current label lane likely uses fill-color or font-weight heuristics that work for solid text but miss outlined variants. Outlined text blueprints have room labels rendered differently at the PDF/vector level — understanding exactly why the current approach fails is half the task.
approach: Pull 2–3 sample blueprint PDFs from outlined-text firms and run them through the current label lane — document where and why it fails
Review the existing label-lane detection logic to understand what signals it uses today (fill color, stroke, font flags)
Identify what distinguishes outlined text in the PDF data (stroke vs fill, opacity, font rendering flags)
Write the v2 vision doc: detection method, confidence threshold, fallback strategy (OCR or manual flag), and edge cases to handle
resources: Takeoff engine repo — label-lane detection module
Sample PDFs from outlined-text client firms
`pdfminer` / `pypdf` docs — text rendering flags and stroke/fill properties
Existing M2 label-lane spec for baseline reference

prep.what: Build the calculation layer that converts each room's assembly data (wall area, floor sqft, ceiling height) into concrete material quantities for paint, drywall, and flooring.
prep.understand: Each room has assembly objects with measured dimensions. You need trade-standard formulas: paint ~350 sqft/gal per coat (typically 2 coats), drywall ~32 sqft per 4×8 board plus waste, flooring sqft plus 10% waste factor. Output should be per-room and with a project aggregate.
approach: Review the assembly data model — confirm what fields are available (wall area, floor sqft, ceiling height) and their units
Define formula constants as named values: `PAINT_COVERAGE = 350`, `DRYWALL_SQFT_PER_BOARD = 32`, `FLOORING_WASTE_FACTOR = 1.10`
Implement `calculate_quantities(room)` returning `{paint_gallons, drywall_boards, flooring_sqft}` per room
Write a unit test with a known room (e.g. 10×12 ft, 9 ft ceiling) and hand-verify output matches expected quantities
resources: Takeoff engine repo — assemblies module and room data model
Trade constants: paint 350 sqft/gal, drywall 32 sqft/board (4×8), flooring +10% waste
Existing fixtures/counts spec for the data model pattern to follow
RSMeans or Craftsman cost data for sanity-checking quantity outputs
